correctness.rationale: For every fixed integer M>=2 and every distinct 0<r1<...<rM<1, polynomial q(x)=(1-x)P(x)-1 has degree exactly M because lambda_M>0 and q(1)=-1. Thus q=-prod_i(x-r_i)/D, D=prod_i(1-r_i), uniquely. Comparing coefficients gives lambda_j=D^-1 sum_{k=0}^{M-j}(-1)^k e_k; the penultimate coefficient imposes sum r_i<1. Conversely e_{k+1}<e_k under sum<1, so each finite alternating partial sum is strictly positive. Factorization yields exactly the target roots, alternating hyperbolicity and correct zero stability parity. Checked 111 exact-rational identity, positivity and boundary assertions independently; finite checks do not prove universality.
